zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Brooklake & Ridgedale District, Briarwood & Convent Station Border
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 1.82%, with an equalization ratio of 86.4%.
Public education represents 58.4% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 31.8%.
Average residential assessment is $656,640, producing an average annual tax bill of $11,950.85.

neighborhoods.name: Brooklake & Ridgedale District
neighborhoods.character: Suburban estates, colonials, and luxury townhomes bordering Brooklake Country Club and NY Jets Atlantic Health Training Center
neighborhoods.description: Affluent borough home to Fairleigh Dickinson University Florham Campus, corporate giants (BASF North America HQ), and NY Jets HQ.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Low certified property tax rate (1.524%) driven by immense corporate, pharmaceutical, and sports facility ratables.

neighborhoods.name: Briarwood & Convent Station Border
neighborhoods.character: Prestigious residential section bordering Morris Township and Convent Station commuter rail, custom colonials
neighborhoods.description: Wooded executive neighborhood with convenient access to midtown direct train commuting.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Enjoys Morris County's lowest composite municipal tax millage.

equityAnalysis.summary: Florham Park Borough maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Florham Park Borough, homeowners pay an average of $11,950.85 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 7.84% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 86.4%, assessed values average ~86.4% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 58.4% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 31.8%, and Morris County claims 9.8%.
